q.t: The area of a parallelogram is:
q.e: Cutting a triangle off one end and moving it to the other turns it into a rectangle with the same base and height.

q.t: The area of a triangle is:
q.e: Two copies of a triangle make a parallelogram with the same base and height.

q.t: Parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels are:
q.e: They share the base and have the same height (the distance between the parallels).

q.t: Find the area of a parallelogram with base 8 cm and height 5 cm (in cm²).
Find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm (in cm²).
A median of a triangle divides it into two triangles of:
q.e: They have equal bases (the median bisects the side) and the same height.

q.t: A triangle and a parallelogram are on the same base and between the same parallels. The area of the triangle is:
o: Half the area of the parallelogram
q.e: Same base and same height, but the triangle has the factor ½.

q.t: Find the area of a rectangle 6 cm by 4 cm (in cm²).
q.e: length × breadth.

q.t: Congruent figures have:
q.e: They fit exactly on each other. (But equal areas do not guarantee congruence.)

q.t: A diagonal of a parallelogram divides it into two triangles that are:
q.e: SSS: opposite sides are equal and the diagonal is common.

q.t: A parallelogram has area 96 cm² and base 12 cm. Find its height (in cm).
q.e: height = area ÷ base.

q.t: A parallelogram has area 60 cm². A triangle stands on the same base between the same parallels. Find the triangle’s area (in cm²).
q.e: Half the parallelogram.

q.t: A parallelogram has sides 10 cm and 6 cm. The altitude on the 10 cm side is 3 cm. Find the altitude on the 6 cm side (in cm).
q.e: The area is the same either way: 10 × 3 = 6 × h.

q.t: A triangle has area 24 cm². A median is drawn. Find the area of each part (in cm²).
q.e: A median halves the area.

q.t: Find the area of a rhombus with diagonals 10 cm and 14 cm (in cm²).
q.e: ½ × d₁ × d₂.

q.t: Parallelogram ABCD has area 80 cm² and P is any point on AB. Find the area of △PDC (in cm²).
q.e: △PDC has the same base DC and the same height as the parallelogram, so it is half of it — wherever P is on AB.

q.t: The diagonals of a parallelogram of area 100 cm² divide it into four triangles. Find the area of each (in cm²).
q.e: Each diagonal halves the area, and the half-diagonals act as medians halving again.

q.t: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 5 cm (in cm²).
The triangle formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of a triangle has what fraction of its area?
q.e: The midpoints split the triangle into four congruent triangles.

q.t: Two triangles on the same base have equal areas (and lie on the same side of it). Then they lie between:
q.e: Equal areas with a common base force equal heights, so the third vertices are on a line parallel to the base.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, AB = 16 cm, the altitude to AB is 8 cm and the altitude to AD is 10 cm. Find AD (in cm).
The three medians of a triangle of area 54 cm² divide it into six small triangles. Find the area of each (in cm²).
q.e: All six have equal areas.

q.t: In △ABC of area 64 cm², D is the midpoint of BC and E is the midpoint of AD. Find the area of △BED (in cm²).
q.e: AD halves the triangle (32), and BE halves △ABD (16).

q.t: Parallelogram ABCD has area 124 cm². E and F are the midpoints of AB and CD. Find the area of AEFD (in cm²).
q.e: EF cuts the parallelogram into two equal parallelograms.

q.t: P is a point inside parallelogram ABCD of area 90 cm². Find area(△APB) + area(△PCD) (in cm²).
q.e: A line through P parallel to AB splits it into two parallelograms; each triangle is half of one of them.

q.t: A rhombus has area 120 cm² and one diagonal 24 cm. Find its side (in cm).
q.e: The other diagonal is 2 × 120 ÷ 24 = 10. Half-diagonals 12 and 5 give side 13.

q.t: In trapezium ABCD with AB ∥ DC, the diagonals meet at O. Which is true?
q.e: △ADC and △BDC have the same base DC and height, so equal areas. Removing the common △ODC leaves △AOD = △BOC.

q.t: The base of a triangle is doubled and its height is halved. Its area:
q.e: ½ × 2b × h/2 = ½bh.

q.t: Parallelogram ABCD has area 72 cm². M is the midpoint of CD. Find the area of △ABM (in cm²).
q.e: Base AB and the full height of the parallelogram — half its area, wherever M is on CD.

q.t: A triangle has base 15 cm and area 90 cm². Find its height (in cm).
G is the centroid of △ABC of area 48 cm². Find the area of △GBC (in cm²).
q.e: The centroid joined to the vertices makes three triangles of equal area.

q.t: Quadrilateral ABCD has diagonal AC = 20 cm, and the perpendiculars from B and D to AC are 6 cm and 9 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: Two triangles on the same base AC: ½ × 20 × (6 + 9).

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD of area 90 cm², E is on BC with BE : EC = 1 : 2. Find the area of △ABE (in cm²).
q.e: △ABC is half the parallelogram (45). △ABE has one third of its base BC and the same height: 15.

q.t: D and E are the midpoints of AB and AC in △ABC. Find the ratio area(△ADE) : area(trapezium DBCE).
q.e: △ADE is one quarter of △ABC, so the trapezium is the other three quarters.

q.t: P is a point on BC with BP : PC = 2 : 3 in △ABC of area 50 cm². Find the area of △ABP (in cm²).
q.e: Triangles with the same height have areas in the ratio of their bases: 2/5 of 50.

q.t: A parallelogram and a rectangle stand on the same base and between the same parallels. Which is true?
o: Equal areas, but the parallelogram has the greater perimeter
The rectangle has the greater area
The parallelogram has the greater area
q.e: Same base and height give equal areas. The parallelogram’s slant sides are longer than the rectangle’s upright sides.

q.t: A trapezium has area 105 cm² and parallel sides 13 cm and 17 cm. Find its height (in cm).
The midpoints of the sides of a square of side 10 cm are joined in order. Find the area of the inner square (in cm²).
q.e: The four corner triangles each have area ½ × 5 × 5 = 12.5, total 50 — half the square.

q.t: The diagonals of parallelogram ABCD meet at O and area(△AOB) = 15 cm². Find the area of ABCD (in cm²).
q.e: The diagonals cut it into four triangles of equal area.

q.t: In △ABC, D is on BC with BD = 2 DC, and E is the midpoint of AD. The area of △ABC is 90 cm². Find the area of △BEC (in cm²).
q.e: E is halfway up AD, so its height above BC is half of A’s. Same base BC, half the height: half the area.
